context.requirement_text: ISS-0816 (queue task 816). CursorPage<T> declares a has_more field. The issue was filed on the premise that lib/letflow/audit.ex emits has_more on the wire, so one CursorPage<T> was covering two incompatible wire shapes. That premise was refuted by ISSUE-FIXER at Step 1 and the issue record docs/issues/ISS-0816.yaml carries the correction inline; the Step 1 audit, not the record, is authoritative. The real defect is that no Letflow route emits has_more at all, so CursorPage<T>.has_more covers zero wire shapes, and two frontend call sites fabricate the field client-side from Boolean(next_cursor). The fix is to delete the field, split the envelope along the axis the backend genuinely varies on (two-key {items, next_cursor} versus three-key {items, next_cursor, count}), retype every call site to the envelope its route actually emits, and record the route-to-shape mapping so it need not be re-derived.

(e) Decision (b)'s asymmetry: confirm the three docblocks on GroupMemberPage, RawAuditPage and TenantListResponse actually say what the design claims, and that leaving TenantListResponse alone is recorded as a deliberate non-change rather than an omission. (f) Decision (d): judge whether keeping modulesApi.list and listShares on the narrowed two-key CursorPage<T> is right given the routes do not exist, and confirm the ISS-0822 provenance comment is specified. (g) T7's new forbidlist.ts PATTERN has-more-wire-field: confirm the two ISS-0821 exemptions are the minimum needed, that adding a PATTERN does not weaken an existing entry, and that the T8 bystander fixture really does contain TimelineFeed's camelCase hasMore. (h) Out-of-scope discipline: ISS-0811, 0812, 0813, 0814, 0815 and the newly filed ISS-0820, 0821, 0822 must not be designed for here; flag any that crept in. result.summary: FAIL. Two BLOCKERs, both measured rather than argued, both in the T7 guard specification. The design is otherwise strong: every claim the dispatch asked to be verified independently held up, including the load-bearing measurement, which reproduced exactly. BLOCKER-1: sections 4 and 7 of the design contradict each other, and the contradiction turns the design's own T3 gate red. Section 4 requires the CursorPage<T> docblock in web/src/types/api.ts to carry 'an explicit statement that no Letflow route emits has_more', naming lib/letflow/routers/audit.ex:308-320, so the next reader does not re-file this. T7 bans the bare token has_more across every web/src/**/*.{ts,tsx,css} file with exactly two exemptions, neither of which is web/src/types/api.ts. Implementing both sections literally puts the banned token in a file the guard scans. BLOCKER-2: T7's exemption list is incomplete. web/src/api/__tests__/identity.groupsApi.test.ts:63 carries the comment 'No `has_more` -- Pagination.Page never emits one.' That file is under web/src/api/__tests__/, which source-scan.spec.ts globs (src/**/*.{ts,tsx,css}, no __tests__ exclusion), it is not in T7's allowedPaths, and section 5 never edits it. The design missed it because section 8 item 8's evidence grep was filtered with grep -v __tests__, while T7 is appliesTo: 'source' and source-scan makes no such exclusion -- the design itself had already recognised in section 5.6 that src/**/__tests__ is inside tsc's scope but did not carry that reasoning across to the guard. Section 8 item 8's conclusion, 'T7's guard is satisfiable with zero exemptions outside __tests__', is therefore false as measured. Both blockers were demonstrated by running the real guard suite in a throwaway worktree with T7 added exactly as section 7 specifies and sections 4 and 5's edits applied: vitest reported 'Source scan found 2 violation(s): has-more-wire-field @ web/src/types/api.ts:14' and 'has-more-wire-field @ web/src/api/__tests__/identity.groupsApi.test.ts:63'. This is the exact failure mode this gate exists to prevent -- an internally inconsistent design reaching implementation, where FRONTEND-DEV would write section 4's docblock, run npm run guards, and discover the design contradicts itself only after the work was done. Everything else passed. The refuted premise (a) is correct and was re-derived from lib/ source. The 6/7 split (b) is correct in all eleven response builders. The measurement (c) reproduced to the character. The scope-widening argument (d) holds against the real code and is justified. Decisions (b)'s asymmetry (e), (d)'s weakest-claim reasoning (f), T8's bystander (g) and out-of-scope discipline (h) all check out. The fix is narrow: reconcile T7's scope with section 4's required docblock and add the missed path, then re-measure rather than assert.

blocking_findings.title: Design section 4 and design section 7 T7 contradict each other; the design's own T3 gate goes red
blocking_findings.where: lib/letflow/design/iss-0816-cursorpage-has-more-audit.md section 4 ('Required docblock content') versus section 7 row T7
blocking_findings.detail: Section 4 states that the CursorPage<T> docblock must carry 'an explicit statement that no Letflow route emits `has_more`, with lib/letflow/routers/audit.ex:308-320 named as the place the internal has_more is dropped, so the next reader does not re-file this'. That docblock lives in web/src/types/api.ts. T7 adds a forbidlist PATTERN named has-more-wire-field with appliesTo: 'source' and a regex matching the bare token has_more on word boundaries, exempting only web/src/pages/promotions/__tests__/PromotionReviewListPage.test.tsx and web/src/pages/tasks/__tests__/TaskInboxPage.test.tsx. web/src/types/api.ts is inside source-scan's glob and is not exempt, so section 4's required sentence is itself a T7 violation. An implementer following section 4 literally makes T3 (npm run guards) fail. Note that the guard reads raw file content with no comment stripping -- web/tests/guards/source-scan.spec.ts findViolationInFile applies the regex to readFileSync content directly -- so a comment counts as a violation exactly as code does.
blocking_findings.measured: Reproduced. In a throwaway worktree at 7751bc81 with T7 added exactly as section 7 specifies and sections 4/5's edits applied, npx vitest run tests/guards/meta-control.spec.ts tests/guards/source-scan.spec.ts reported: 'Source scan found 2 violation(s): has-more-wire-field @ web/src/types/api.ts:14 ...' with 1 test file failed, 48 of 49 tests passing.
blocking_findings.must_change: Resolve the contradiction explicitly, in one of three ways, and state which was chosen and why: (i) narrow T7's regex so it matches only the code form of the field -- an object-literal key or a property access, e.g. has_more followed by a colon or preceded by a dot -- rather than any occurrence of the token, which preserves the guard's real purpose (stopping the field from reappearing on the wire contract) while allowing prose that names it; or (ii) add web/src/types/api.ts to T7's allowedPaths, which is the weakest option because api.ts is precisely the file the guard most needs to cover and exempting it guts the guard; or (iii) reword section 4's required docblock so it does not contain the literal token, which must then be stated as a deliberate trade-off, because section 4's stated purpose is to name the field so the issue is not re-filed, and a docblock that cannot name it serves that purpose worse. Whichever is chosen must be re-measured by actually running npm run guards, not asserted -- the design's existing measurement is what missed this.

blocking_findings.title: T7's exemption list is incomplete: web/src/api/__tests__/identity.groupsApi.test.ts:63 is an unhandled violation
blocking_findings.where: lib/letflow/design/iss-0816-cursorpage-has-more-audit.md section 7 row T7 and section 8 item 8
blocking_findings.detail: web/src/api/__tests__/identity.groupsApi.test.ts:63 reads ' *  No `has_more` -- Pagination.Page never emits one. */'. It is a truthful comment documenting the absence of the field, not a defect, and section 5 does not edit that file. web/tests/guards/source-scan.spec.ts globs 'src/**/*.{ts,tsx,css}' relative to web/ with no __tests__ exclusion, so the file is scanned; T7 is appliesTo: 'source' and does not exempt it. Root cause of the miss: section 8 item 8's evidence grep was 'grep -rn has_more web/src --include=*.ts --include=*.tsx | grep -v __tests__', which filtered the file out, and the design then concluded 'T7's guard is satisfiable with zero exemptions outside __tests__'. That conclusion is false as measured, and the design had the information to catch it -- section 5.6 already reasons correctly that tsconfig.app.json's include: ["src"] puts src/**/__tests__ inside npm run type-check, but that reasoning was not carried across to the guard, whose glob has the same property.
blocking_findings.measured: Reproduced in the same worktree run: 'has-more-wire-field @ web/src/api/__tests__/identity.groupsApi.test.ts:63' was the second of the two reported violations.
blocking_findings.must_change: Either add web/src/api/__tests__/identity.groupsApi.test.ts to T7's allowedPaths (with a comment saying why, and noting it is NOT an ISS-0821 fixture so it is not removed when ISS-0821 lands, unlike the other two exemptions), or adopt BLOCKER-1 resolution (i), whose narrowed code-form regex clears this comment as well as api.ts's docblock in one move -- option (i) resolves both blockers together and is the recommended shape. Additionally, correct section 8 item 8: re-run its grep WITHOUT the grep -v __tests__ filter, since T7's actual scan scope includes __tests__, and restate the conclusion from the corrected measurement.

independent_verification.claim: (a) The refuted premise -- no Letflow route emits has_more
independent_verification.evidence: Re-derived from lib/ source, not inherited. lib/letflow/audit.ex:276 is the @spec of list_entries/1 declaring {:ok, %{items: [Entry.t()], has_more: boolean()}}; :295 splits the page and :297 returns that internal map -- an in-process return, never HTTP. lib/letflow/routers/audit.ex:203-204 is 'defp render_page(conn, {:ok, %{items: items, has_more: has_more}}) do / Response.ok(conn, page_body(items, next_cursor(items, has_more)))' -- the internal has_more is consumed as an argument to next_cursor/2 and never forwarded. page_body/2 at :308-320 hand-builds exactly %{"items" => items, "next_cursor" => next_cursor, "count" => length(items)} under an '-- Response allowlist (INV-2) --' banner. Widened beyond the named lines: grep for '"has_more"', 'has_more =>' and ':has_more' across all of lib/*.ex returns zero matches, so no map destined for Jason encoding carries the key under either a string or an atom spelling. Only four lib files mention the token at all -- audit.ex and routers/audit.ex (above), routers/dlq.ex:79 (a comment asserting the body is exactly two keys, consistent), and event_store.ex (read_global/1 at :1053 returns an internal has_more, but grep for 'read_global(' across lib/ excluding event_store.ex itself returns zero callers, so it cannot reach HTTP). The design's central premise is sound and the deletion-plus-split correction follows from it.

independent_verification.claim: (b) The two-key/three-key split -- 6 routes/7 call sites versus 7 routes
independent_verification.evidence: All eleven response builders re-read at HEAD, both sides of the split, not a sample. Two-key {items, next_cursor}: definitions.ex:454-458 render_list_result/2 and :539-544 render_search_result/2, services.ex:131-135 handle_list_result/2, admin_services.ex:198-202 handle_list_result/2, promotions.ex:944-948 render_list_reviews/2, dlq.ex:140-144 handle_list_result/2 -- every one hand-builds exactly the two string keys. Three-key {items, next_cursor, count}: audit.ex:308-320 and instances.ex:954-959 render_page_result/3 and tasks.ex:269-275 handle_list_result/2 all hand-build the three string keys with "count" => length(items); api/pagination.ex:81 carries @derive {Jason.Encoder, only: [:items, :next_cursor, :count]} on the Page struct, and page_response/2 at :171-173 builds %Page{items: items, next_cursor: next_cursor, count: length(items)}; identity.ex:552 calls Pagination.page_response/2 for group members. No site is assigned the wrong shape. The count-is-length(items)-not-a-total invariant (INV-B) is borne out by every three-key builder.

independent_verification.claim: (c) Deleting api.ts:17 alone yields exactly four TS2353 errors; promotions.ts:265 does not error
independent_verification.evidence: Method: git worktree add --detach to a scratchpad path at 7751bc81 (confirmed git diff --name-only e512c53a 7751bc81 -- web/ is empty, so web/ is identical to the tree the design measured), node_modules supplied by a directory junction so nothing in the working checkout was touched. Baseline ./node_modules/.bin/tsc -b tsconfig.json --force exited 0. Then sed -i '17d' src/types/api.ts, removing only 'has_more: boolean' from CursorPage<T> and leaving items and next_cursor, and re-ran tsc -b --force. Result: exit 2, exactly four errors, all TS2353, at src/api/audit.ts(71,7), src/pages/dlq/__tests__/DlqPage.pagination.test.tsx(78,63), (79,64) and (80,58) -- the count, the error code and all four file/line/column positions match CODE-DESIGNER's section 8 item 2 to the character. promotions.ts:265 did NOT appear in the error set, confirming section 8 item 3: the object literal in the .then callback's return position is not excess-property-checked there. The scope boundary therefore stands as drawn -- section 5.6's DlqPage.pagination.test.tsx edit is a genuine hard compile blocker and is correctly in scope while the other three ISS-0821 sites are correctly out, and the promotions.ts:265 removal is correctly characterised as a correctness/clarity edit under decision (a) rather than a compile requirement.

independent_verification.claim: (d) Decision (c)'s scope-widening -- GroupsPage is a wrong write path, so AC3's truncation-notice branch is unavailable
independent_verification.verdict: CONFIRMED -- the wider scope is justified
independent_verification.evidence: Verified line by line against the real code, and every line citation in the design is exact. web/src/api/identity.ts:62-63 is 'members: (id: string) => client.get<GroupMemberPage>(`/api/v1/identity/groups/${id}/members`)' -- no cursor, no page_size, so the request takes the server default. GroupsPage.tsx:56 is the queryFn calling groupsApi.members(activeGroupId); :60 is 'const members = useMemo(() => membersPage?.items ?? [], [membersPage?.items])'; next_cursor appears nowhere in the file. The server default is 50 (lib/letflow/api/pagination.ex:51 @default_page_size 50, reached via identity.ex:546-548 parse_page_size_param(nil) then validate_page_size(nil)). GroupsPage.tsx:103-110 is 'const availableUsers = useMemo(() => { const list = users?.items ?? []; const memberIds = new Set(members.map((user) => user.id)); return list.filter((user) => { const id = user.id ?? user.user_id ?? ''; return id !== '' && !memberIds.has(id) }) }, [members, users?.items])' -- memberIds is built from the TRUNCATED members array, so every member from the 51st on is absent from the set and passes the filter. :203-206 maps availableUsers into the Add-member <option> list, and :216 fires addMember.mutate({ groupId, userId: selectedUserId }) into POST /api/v1/identity/groups/:id/members. The chain the design describes is real and complete. Decisive point for AC3: the truncation notice would sit on the 'Current members' list (heading at :224), while the defect is in a DIFFERENT control -- the dropdown, which is derived from users minus members. A notice on the member list cannot make the set difference correct, so AC3's 'or explicitly states the list is truncated' branch genuinely does not close this. Keeping the drain in scope is justified, and INV-D states the right general rule. The design's T6 is correctly aimed: it asserts that u-51 is not rendered as an <option>, i.e. on the dropdown rather than on the write, which is the assertion that actually holds regardless of backend behaviour.

independent_verification.claim: (d, second part) The 20-request cap and the truncated escape hatch are precise enough to build
independent_verification.verdict: ADEQUATE, with one clarifying sentence recommended
independent_verification.evidence: Section 6.1 gives fully specified signatures -- members: (id: string, params?: { cursor?: string; page_size?: number }) => Promise<GroupMemberPage> and listAllMembers: (id: string) => Promise<{ items: GroupMember[]; truncated: boolean }> -- plus a five-point behavioural contract: page_size 200 (verified: lib/letflow/api/pagination.ex:50 @max_page_size 200, so 200 really is the server maximum), feed each next_cursor into the next cursor, stop on null and concatenate in request order, stop early after 20 requests returning truncated: true, and reject on the first failed request so useQuery's existing error handling is unchanged. The error shape is therefore specified. GroupMember is exported at web/src/types/api.ts:462 and is NOT currently imported by identity.ts (whose import block at :2-13 brings in GroupMemberPage but not GroupMember), so the design's conditional 'GroupMember must be imported into identity.ts if it is not already' resolves to: yes, add it. Not blocking. The one soft edge: the behaviour when the 20th request returns next_cursor === null is resolvable from the text ('truncated is false on every normal termination', and reaching a null cursor is a normal termination) but is not stated outright, and under this project's weak-model-tolerance constraint a literal implementer could set truncated: true there. Recommend one explicit sentence: truncated is true if and only if the loop stopped because the request cap was reached while next_cursor was still non-null.

independent_verification.claim: (e) Decision (b)'s asymmetry -- the three docblocks say what the design claims
independent_verification.evidence: web/src/types/api.ts:473-476, GroupMemberPage: '`Letflow.Api.Pagination.Page`'s encoder shape (`lib/letflow/api/pagination.ex:81`, `@derive {Jason.Encoder, only: [:items, :next_cursor, :count]}`). Not `CursorPage<T>`, which declares a `has_more` the backend never emits.' The quoted sentence is exactly at :475-476 as the design cites, and the fix falsifies it, so the docblock must change regardless -- the alias is the cheaper correct edit and retaining the exported name means identity.ts:7 and :63 are untouched, as claimed. web/src/api/audit.ts:37-41, RawAuditPage: declared without export, so module-private as claimed, and character-for-character the three-key shape {items: RawAuditEntry[]; next_cursor: string | null; count: number}. web/src/api/tenants.ts:18-26, TenantListResponse: the comment cites the same @derive and says 'There has never been a `total`/`limit`/`offset` field on this endpoint's response body', with an inline note that count is 'length(items) for the CURRENT PAGE ONLY -- never a cross-page total'. It does not mention has_more anywhere, so nothing in this fix falsifies it and the stated rule 'edit what the fix falsifies, leave alone what it does not' is applied consistently across all three. The non-change is properly recorded: section 3(b) calls it 'a deliberate non-change, so a future reader does not read it as an oversight', and section 8 item 7 records that collapsing it was actually tried and type-checks clean, making it a scope choice rather than a technical constraint. That is an omission correctly converted into a documented decision. Also confirmed for completeness: EntityRecordsPage's docblock at api.ts:370-373 does state that reusing CursorPage<T> 'would silently claim a field the API never sends', so decision (e)'s collapse follows from the same rule and CODE-DESIGNER correctly self-flagged it as a widening in its own handoff issues.

independent_verification.claim: (f) Decision (d) -- keep modulesApi.list/.listShares on the narrowed two-key CursorPage<T>
independent_verification.evidence: web/src/api/modules.ts:44 types list as CursorPage<ProcessModuleCatalogEntry> against /api/v1/admin/modules and :61 types listShares as CursorPage<ModuleShare> against /api/v1/admin/module-shares -- both line citations exact. lib/letflow/router.ex:82 lists Letflow.Routers.ProcessModules against process_modules.zig as deferred to S5, and no file matching *module* exists under lib/letflow/routers/, so the routes genuinely have no server and there is no ground truth to derive from. The reasoning is right on its own terms: both candidate envelopes contain items and next_cursor, so a consumer written against the two-key shape stays correct whichever S5 ships, whereas CountedCursorPage<T> would assert a count nothing has ever sent -- which would re-create, on the only two routes with no server at all, the exact defect this run exists to remove. It is also the option that requires no edit once section 4 narrows CursorPage<T>, so it minimises the diff as well as the claim. The provenance comment is specified concretely in section 5.5: one comment above each of :44 and :61 recording that the routes have no server, citing router.ex:82 and the S5 deferral, naming ISS-0822, and stating that CursorPage<T> here is the deliberate weakest claim pending the route's arrival rather than a verified shape. That is enough for an implementer to write it.

independent_verification.claim: (g) T7's guard -- exemption minimality, no weakening of existing entries, and the T8 bystander
independent_verification.verdict: SPLIT -- two of three confirmed, exemption minimality FAILS (see BLOCKER-1 and BLOCKER-2)
independent_verification.evidence: No weakening of existing entries: CONFIRMED. web/tests/guards/forbidlist.ts exports PATTERNS as a flat GuardPattern[] whose entries are independent records of name/regex/appliesTo/allowedPaths/rationale; appending an entry changes no existing entry's regex or allowedPaths. meta-control.spec.ts's single-source-regex invariant applies only to source-scan.spec.ts and bundle-scan.spec.ts, not to forbidlist.ts, so a new regex literal in forbidlist.ts is legal. No test asserts PATTERNS.length or snapshots the array. Measured: the worktree run showed all ten pre-existing patterns still passing their own offender/bystander assertions with T7 added. T8's bystander: CONFIRMED, and the design's mechanical guarantee works. web/src/components/instances/TimelineFeed.tsx:7 declares 'hasMore: boolean', used at :15 and :37, and web/src/pages/instances/InstanceDetailPage.tsx:369 passes 'hasMore={Boolean(timelineQuery.data?.next_cursor)}' -- exactly the camelCase prop derived from next_cursor that the design says must not be touched and must not match. meta-control.spec.ts does iterate every PATTERNS entry and require both an offender fixture the regex matches and a bystander fixture it does not, so T8 is a real mechanical requirement rather than a convention; measured with a bystander fixture containing the TimelineFeed line, 'has-more-wire-field > regex does NOT match bystander' passed. Exemption minimality: FAILS -- the two listed exemptions are necessary but not sufficient. Two further source-scan violations exist, one of them created by the design's own section 4. See BLOCKER-1 and BLOCKER-2.

Section 10 tabulates ISS-0820, ISS-0821, ISS-0822, ISS-0813 and the ISS-0811/0812/0814/0815 group as filed-not-fixed, and nothing in sections 3 through 6 designs a fix for any of them. The single crossing is web/src/pages/dlq/__tests__/DlqPage.pagination.test.tsx:78-80, one of ISS-0821's four fixtures, and it is justified by measurement rather than convenience -- I reproduced the TS2353 errors at exactly those three positions, so it is a genuine hard compile blocker for AC4 and would fall under core-directives.md's Unblock-Everything rather than scope creep. The other three ISS-0821 sites are correctly left untouched and the reason is correct as stated: PromotionReviewListPage.test.tsx:119/:270 and TaskInboxPage.test.tsx:134/:160 pass through as-unknown casts or untyped vi.fn(), so excess-property checking never applies, and web/tests/e2e/obs04.timeline.e2e.spec.ts is outside tsconfig's include: ["src"] -- and, separately verified, also outside source-scan's 'src/**' glob, so it needs no T7 exemption either. CODE-DESIGNER also self-flagged the one genuine widening (EntityRecordsPage, decision (e)) in its own handoff issues rather than letting it pass unremarked, and correctly routed the newly found usersApi.list finding to ORCH for id allocation instead of filing it itself; ORCH has since filed it as ISS-0823 in commit ea1a43a4, so section 10's '(unfiled)' row can be updated to name ISS-0823 on the next revision.

issues.description: Design sections 4 and 7 T7 contradict each other. Section 4 requires the CursorPage<T> docblock in web/src/types/api.ts to state that no Letflow route emits has_more; T7 bans that token across web/src with only two exemptions, neither of which covers api.ts. Measured in a throwaway worktree: source-scan reports 'has-more-wire-field @ web/src/types/api.ts:14'. The design's own T3 (npm run guards) goes red on a literal implementation. See result.blocking_findings BLOCKER-1 for the three resolution options and which is recommended.

T7's allowedPaths is incomplete. web/src/api/__tests__/identity.groupsApi.test.ts:63 carries the truthful comment 'No `has_more` -- Pagination.Page never emits one.' and is inside source-scan's 'src/**/*.{ts,tsx,css}' glob, which has no __tests__ exclusion. The design missed it because section 8 item 8's evidence grep was filtered with grep -v __tests__ while T7 is appliesTo: 'source'. Measured: source-scan reports it as the second violation. Section 8 item 8's conclusion that the guard is satisfiable with zero exemptions outside __tests__ is false as measured and must be re-run without that filter. See result.blocking_findings BLOCKER-2.

Line-citation error. Design section 3(c) cites 'lib/letflow/api/pagination.ex:53 @default_page_size 50'. The actual line is 51 (@max_page_size 200 is at :50, @default_page_size 50 at :51). The value 50 is correct and the argument is unaffected; only the line number is wrong. Section 6.1's citation of pagination.ex:50 for @max_page_size 200 is correct.

Severity nuance in decision (c) worth recording so the next reader does not over-rate it. web/src/types/api.ts:498-502 defines GroupMemberAddResult with a 'created: boolean' field, which means the backend add-member path is idempotent and re-adding an existing member is not destructive. The design's framing 'that is a wrong write path, not a wrong display' is therefore stronger than the evidence strictly supports. The conclusion is unaffected and the wider scope remains justified, but on the INV-D ground the design also states -- a control that computes a set difference must hold the complete collection -- rather than on write destructiveness. Recommend one sentence noting the idempotency, so a later reader weighing whether to defer this work has the real severity. The test matrix is already correctly aimed: T6 asserts on the dropdown, not on the mutation.

Soft edge in the drain contract. Section 6.1 does not state outright what truncated should be when the 20th request returns next_cursor === null. It is resolvable from 'truncated is false on every normal termination', but under this project's weak-model-tolerance constraint it should be stated explicitly: truncated is true if and only if the loop stopped because the request cap was reached while next_cursor was still non-null.

Housekeeping for the next revision. Design section 10's last row reads '(unfiled)' for the GroupsPage usersApi.list finding. ORCH has since filed it as ISS-0823 (commit ea1a43a4, docs/issues/ISS-0823.yaml), so that row can now name the id. Not a defect in the design as written -- CODE-DESIGNER correctly reported the finding to ORCH rather than allocating an id itself, per core-directives.md 'No Issue Left Local-Only'.

what_must_change: 1. Reconcile T7 with section 4's required docblock. Preferred: narrow T7's regex from the bare token to the code form of the field (an object-literal key or property access), so the guard still stops the field reappearing on the wire contract while prose may name it. Alternatives, if rejected, must be stated with the trade-off: exempt web/src/types/api.ts (weakest -- it guts the guard's most important file), or reword section 4 to avoid the literal token (which costs section 4 its stated purpose of naming the field so the issue is not re-filed).

2. Handle web/src/api/__tests__/identity.groupsApi.test.ts:63. Either the narrowed regex from item 1 clears it (recommended -- one change resolves both blockers), or add it to allowedPaths with a comment noting it is not an ISS-0821 fixture and therefore is not removed when ISS-0821 lands, unlike the other two exemptions.

3. Correct section 8 item 8. Re-run its grep WITHOUT the 'grep -v __tests__' filter, since T7's actual scan scope includes src/**/__tests__, and restate the conclusion from the corrected measurement rather than from the filtered one.

4. Re-measure, do not assert. Whatever shape items 1 and 2 take, run npm run guards with T7 actually present and quote the real output in section 8. The existing section 8 is otherwise a model of how to evidence a design, which is why the one filtered grep is worth correcting rather than papering over.
5. Fix the section 3(c) line citation: @default_page_size 50 is at lib/letflow/api/pagination.ex:51, not :53.
6. Add the truncated edge-case sentence to section 6.1: truncated is true if and only if the request cap was reached while next_cursor was still non-null.

7. Add one sentence to decision (c) noting GroupMemberAddResult.created (web/src/types/api.ts:498-502) makes the backend add idempotent, so the defect's severity rests on the availableUsers set difference (INV-D) rather than on a destructive write. The decision itself stands.
8. Update section 10's '(unfiled)' row to name ISS-0823.
